plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly one's private value. In this single-round auction with $20 as my value, bidding $20 ensures I won't overpay if I win, and prevents me from losing potential profit by bidding too low. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-time game, strategic complexity is reduced. I'll follow the economists' recommendation and bid my true value.

Economic theory suggests bidding one's true value ($29) is the dominant strategy in a first-price sealed-bid auction. Since values are independently drawn and this is a single round, strategic complexity is reduced. Bidding below value risks losing the item, while bidding above risks negative payoff. Without repeated interaction history, the safest approach is to bid exactly my private value of $29, which maximizes potential profit by balancing winning probability and cost.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $45. This is because:

2. Bidding more than my value could lead to negative payoff
3. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, truthful bidding maximizes expected personal profit
